title: DIVINE
text: DIVINE package offers collection curated datasets along convenient data management functions. sample datasets (e.g., patient demographics, symptoms, treatments, outcomes) included demonstration purposes, enabling users practice test various data manipulation workflows. Using DIVINE functions, can inspect, clean, merge, summarize, visualize, export data efficiently. vignette, illustrate common tasks functions provided DIVINE help streamline data analysis process.

title: DIVINE
text: impute_missing() function lets replace missing values using specific strategy. provide named list formulas (<selector> ~ <strategy>), <selector> can tidyselect expression (e.g. column name, starts_with(), (.numeric)) <strategy> one following strategies: “mean” “median” (numeric columns ) “mode” (character/factor columns ) numeric constant (numeric columns) character constant (character/factor columns) can also drop rows entirely NA setting all_na_rm = TRUE. running impute_missing(), returned dataset missing values replaced columns specified according chosen strategies. overall dataset structure (column names types) preserved possible; number rows change set drop_all_na = TRUE.
code: # 1) Default: replace all numeric NAs with column means cleaned_default <- impute_missing(icu)  # 2) Single column strategies: #    - Mean for vent_mec_start_days #    - Zero for icu_enter_days cleaned_mix <- impute_missing(   icu,   method = list(     vent_mec_start_days ~ "mean",     icu_enter_days ~ 0   ) )  # 3) Multiple columns at once: #    - Medians for any column ending in "_days" cleaned_days_median <- impute_missing(   icu,   method = list(starts_with(".*_days$") ~ "median") )  # 4) Factor/character imputation: #    - Fill gender with its most common level #    - Fill status with "Unknown" cleaned_char <- impute_missing(   icu,   method = list(     covid_wave ~ "mode",     icu ~ "Unknown"   ) )  # 5) Drop all-NA rows first, then impute numeric means cleaned_no_empty <- impute_missing(   icu,   method    = list(where(is.numeric) ~ "mean"),   drop_all_na = TRUE ) # ▶ message: Removed X rows where all values were NA

title: DIVINE
text: working related tables, multi_join() combines several data frames single table common key. Choose join behavior join_type = "left", "inner", "right", "full" control rows kept. example, suppose demographic, vital signs, scores tables sharing default key variables package (record_id, covid_wave, center): creates one combined data frame joined includes rows demographic matches information vital_signs scores record_id. Use join_type decide whether unmatched rows one tables retained.
code: data("vital_signs") data("scores")  joined <- multi_join(   list(demographic, vital_signs, scores),   key = c("record_id", "covid_wave", "center"),   join_type = "left" )

title: DIVINE
text: Use stats_table() generate summary tables (leveraging gtsummary package) one variables, optionally stratified grouping variable. Use statistic_type argument select summary: “mean_sd” (show mean (SD) numeric variables) “median_iqr” (show median [Q1; Q3]) “” (include mean (SD) median [Q1; Q3] applicable) tbl object gtsummary-style table can print, refine export reports. Set pvalue = TRUE add p-values group comparisons, consult function documentation options format labels missing-value displays.
code: # Mean (SD) by group (e.g., by gender or cohort) tbl1 <- stats_table(   demographic,   vars = c("age", "smoker", "alcohol"),   by = "sex",   statistic_type = "mean_sd",   pvalue = TRUE )  # Median [Q1; Q3] for all observations (no grouping) tbl2 <- stats_table(   demographic,   statistic_type = "median_iqr" )  # Both mean (SD) and median [IQR] combined tbl3 <- stats_table(   demographic,   statistic_type = "both" )

title: DIVINE
text: Create common plot types quickly multi_plot(). supports histograms, density plots, boxplots, barplots, spider (radar) charts. instance:    call generates plot (using ggplot2 hood). Customize titles, colors, variables needed data.
code: # Histogram of age multi_plot(   demographic,   x = "age",   plot_type = "histogram",   fill_color = "skyblue",   title = "Distribution of Age" ) # Boxplot of age by sex multi_plot(   demographic,   x = "sex",   y = "age",   plot_type = "boxplot",   group = "sex",   title = "Age by Sex" ) # Spider plot of numeric variables (e.g., compare age, weight, height distributions) multi_plot(   comorbidities,   radar = c("hypertension", "dyslipidemia", "depression", "mild_kidney_disease", "dm"),   radar_labels = stringr::str_to_sentence(c("hypertension", "dyslipidemia", "depression", "mild_kidney_disease", "dm")),   radar_color = "blue",   radar_ref_lev = "Yes",   plot_type = "spider" )

title: DIVINE
text: Finally, use export_data() save processed data disk various formats. Supported formats include CSV, XLSX, RDS, Rdata, SPSS, Stata, SAS: Specify path including filename extension; function write file accordingly. can also use format = "rds" (R), "Rdata" (R), "sav" (SPSS), "dta" (Stata), "sas7bdat" (SAS) needed.
code: # Export cleaned data to CSV export_data(cleaned_default, format = "csv", path = "cleaned_demographic.csv")  # Export joined data to Excel export_data(joined, format = "xlsx", path = "joined_data.xlsx")

title: Replace Missing Values — impute_missing

title: Replace Missing Values — impute_missing
